title: Authentication service returning 503 errors
body: The authentication service may return HTTP 503 Service Unavailable errors during peak load or when dependent services are degraded. Root cause is typically one of three things: the token validation cache is exhausted, the upstream identity provider is unreachable, or the service pod has exceeded its connection pool limit. Resolution steps: first, check the auth-service health endpoint at /internal/health. If the cache is the issue, restart the auth-service pod to flush the in-memory token store. If the identity provider is unreachable, verify network policies and confirm the IDP certificate has not expired. For connection pool exhaustion, increase MAX_POOL_SIZE in the service configuration and redeploy. If the 503 persists beyond 5 minutes, escalate to the platform team with the correlation ID from the response header.

title: Mobile app crashes on startup
body: The mobile application may crash immediately on launch due to a corrupted local data cache or an incompatible configuration file left from a previous version. This affects iOS and Android builds. To resolve: first, clear the application cache via Settings > App > Clear Cache. If the crash persists, perform a clean uninstall and reinstall — this resets the on-device SQLite database without affecting cloud-stored user data. For users on Android 12 or below, an additional manifest permission for SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM must be granted manually after install. Developers investigating crash reports should check Crashlytics for the stack trace; the most common failure point is the AppInitializer class when SharedPreferences is null on first launch after an OS upgrade.

title: Recurring billing charge after subscription cancellation
body: Customers may see a billing charge after cancelling their subscription if the cancellation was processed after the billing cycle cutoff time. Our billing system processes renewals at 00:00 UTC on the renewal date. Cancellations submitted within 24 hours before renewal may not propagate in time to prevent the charge. Resolution: verify the cancellation timestamp in the billing dashboard. If cancellation preceded the charge, issue a full refund via the Stripe dashboard using the charge ID from the customer record. For partial-period cancellations, apply a prorated credit to the next invoice rather than a refund. Prevent recurrence by ensuring cancellation webhooks from the subscription service reach the billing service within the 48-hour window before renewal.

title: Password reset email not delivered
body: Users who do not receive a password reset email should first check their spam or junk folder, as transactional emails from our sending domain may be filtered by aggressive spam rules. If the email is not in spam, verify the email address on the account matches what the user is checking — accounts created via OAuth have the OAuth provider email, not a separately entered address. Our email provider SendGrid delivers within 2 minutes under normal conditions; delays beyond 5 minutes indicate a delivery issue. In that case, check the SendGrid activity feed for bounces or blocks. Common causes: the user's domain has a strict DMARC policy, or the address was previously marked as spam by the user. Resolution: remove the address from the SendGrid suppression list and resend.

title: Two-factor authentication setup and recovery
body: Two-factor authentication (2FA) can be enabled via Account Settings > Security > Enable 2FA. We support TOTP-based authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password) and SMS as a fallback. During setup, scan the QR code with your authenticator app and confirm with the 6-digit TOTP code before saving. Store the 10 backup recovery codes in a secure location — they are shown once. If a user loses access to their authenticator and has no backup codes, identity verification is required: submit a support ticket with a government-issued ID. For enterprise accounts with SSO, 2FA is managed by the identity provider and cannot be configured in-app. Disabling 2FA requires re-entering the current TOTP code as confirmation.

title: Account locked after repeated failed login attempts
body: Accounts are automatically locked after 10 consecutive failed login attempts within a 15-minute window. This is a security measure to prevent brute-force attacks. A locked account cannot authenticate until unlocked, regardless of whether the correct credentials are entered. The account owner receives an email notification at the time of lockout. To unlock: the account owner can click the unlock link in the notification email, valid for 30 minutes. If the link has expired, an administrator can unlock the account via the Admin Console under Users > Account Status. The lockout counter resets on successful login. Repeated lockouts from the same IP address are escalated to the security team automatically via a Datadog alert.

title: Subscription plan upgrade and downgrade procedures
body: Users can change their subscription plan at any time via Account > Billing > Change Plan. Upgrades take effect immediately and are prorated: the remaining days on the current plan are credited, and the new plan price is charged for the remainder of the billing period. Downgrades take effect at the end of the current billing period — the user retains current-plan features until the renewal date. Downgrading from an annual plan mid-term generates a prorated credit note rather than a refund, applied to the next invoice. If a user has been overcharged due to a failed downgrade, verify the subscription state in Stripe and manually apply the credit. Enterprise plans with committed usage cannot be downgraded without account manager approval.

title: Data export and GDPR deletion requests
body: Users in GDPR-regulated regions can request a full export of their personal data or a deletion of their account under the right to data portability and the right to erasure. To request an export: navigate to Account > Privacy > Download My Data. A ZIP archive is prepared within 72 hours and sent to the account email. For deletion requests, submit via Account > Privacy > Delete Account or by contacting support. Deletion is irreversible and removes all user-generated content, preferences, and identifiers. A 30-day grace period applies before permanent deletion to allow recovery of accidental requests. For enterprise accounts, the data controller (company admin) must submit deletion requests on behalf of users per the data processing agreement.

title: API rate limiting and quota management
body: The REST API enforces per-account rate limits to ensure fair usage. Default limits are 1,000 requests per minute for standard accounts and 10,000 for enterprise. Requests that exceed the limit receive a 429 Too Many Requests response with a Retry-After header indicating when the limit resets. To check current usage, call GET /v1/quota. Rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset) are returned on every API response. If your integration is hitting limits legitimately, request a quota increase via the developer portal. For sudden unexplained 429 errors, check whether another integration or automation is sharing the same API key. Use separate API keys per integration to isolate quota consumption.

title: Mobile app offline mode and sync behaviour
body: The mobile app supports offline access for previously loaded content. When connectivity is lost, the app switches to offline mode automatically, indicated by an orange banner in the navigation bar. In offline mode, users can view and edit content cached in the last sync. Changes made offline are queued locally and synced when connectivity is restored. Conflict resolution uses a last-write-wins strategy based on device timestamp. If a sync fails repeatedly after connectivity is restored, force a manual sync via Settings > Sync > Sync Now. In rare cases where the local database is corrupted, clearing the app cache (Settings > App > Clear Cache) and re-syncing will rebuild the local store from the server.

title: Payment method update failure
body: Updating a payment method may fail for several reasons: the new card has been declined by the issuer, the card number has been entered incorrectly, or the billing address does not match the card record. When a payment method update fails, the existing method remains active — no service interruption occurs. To resolve: ask the user to verify card details and try again. If the card is being declined despite correct details, they should contact their bank as the issuer may be blocking the transaction. For enterprise accounts with purchase order invoicing, payment method changes require approval from the finance team. Stripe webhook events PAYMENT_METHOD_UPDATED and PAYMENT_METHOD_ATTACH_FAILED are logged for all update attempts.

title: Single sign-on (SSO) configuration with SAML 2.0
body: Enterprise accounts can configure SAML 2.0-based single sign-on via Admin Console > Security > SSO Configuration. Required fields: identity provider entity ID, SSO URL, and X.509 certificate. Our service provider metadata is available at /auth/saml/metadata. After saving the SSO configuration, initiate a test login before enforcing SSO for the entire organization — use the Test SSO button to validate the SAML assertion without locking out existing users. Common misconfiguration: the NameID format must be set to emailAddress; persistent or transient NameID formats will fail user lookup. When SSO is enforced, password-based login is disabled for all non-admin members. Admins retain password login as a break-glass fallback.

title: Webhook delivery failures and retry policy
body: Webhook endpoints that return a non-2xx HTTP status or fail to respond within 10 seconds are considered delivery failures. Our system retries failed webhooks with exponential backoff: 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, 6 hours. After 5 failed attempts, the webhook is disabled and the account contact receives an email notification. To re-enable a disabled webhook, verify that the endpoint is accessible and returning 200, then re-enable via API Console > Webhooks > Manage. Webhook payloads are signed with HMAC-SHA256 using the webhook secret — always verify the X-Webhook-Signature header before processing. Common failure causes: endpoint returning 302 redirects (not followed), SSL certificate errors, or firewall blocking our IP range (documented at /docs/ip-allowlist).

title: User roles and permission management
body: Access control is managed through role-based permissions. Built-in roles are Owner, Admin, Member, and Viewer. Owners can manage billing and delete the organization. Admins can manage members and configure integrations but cannot access billing. Members have full access to workspace content. Viewers have read-only access. Custom roles can be created via Admin Console > Roles for enterprise accounts. Permissions are additive — a user with multiple roles receives the union of all role permissions. When a user's role is changed, the new permissions take effect immediately and existing sessions are updated within 60 seconds via token refresh. Audit logs of all permission changes are retained for 90 days and accessible via Admin Console > Audit Log.

title: Browser extension compatibility and troubleshooting
body: The official browser extension is supported on Chrome 110+, Firefox 115+, and Edge 110+. Safari is not supported. The extension requires the following permissions: storage, activeTab, and identity. If the extension fails to load after installation, check that browser extensions are not blocked by enterprise device management policy. Common issues: extension conflicts with ad blockers that intercept network requests — whitelist our domain in uBlock Origin or similar tools. If the extension icon shows an error badge, click it to view the error code: E001 means the user is not authenticated (sign in to the web app first), E002 means the extension cannot reach the API (check network/proxy settings). Clearing extension storage via chrome://extensions > Details > Clear Storage resolves most persistent state issues.
